title: Before the walls of Barshalūna the sultan breaks the army of Arghūn. Saʿd commands in person and gives the right wing, with two-thirds of the horse, to his brother Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī. The heavy infantry holds the centre while the wings destroy the Aragonese flanks, and then close on the levies left in the middle. 3,375 of theirs fall for 1,228 of ours (+21 war score)
source: Trent's account and battle screens of 29 January and 19 February 1374

title: The sultan rides down what is left of the Aragonese army at Ṭarrakūna: 1,343 of theirs killed or taken for 31 of ours (+6 war score). By 9 March all that remains of the host of Arghūn is 161 levies somewhere in the mountains
source: Trent's account and battle screen of 9 March 1374

title: While the army is in Catalonia, the rebuilding goes on at home: the treasury is paying for a Royal Court in Gharnāṭa, mines at Almonaster (El-Mnastir), and the second level of a ṯaġr fort at Aracena (Eš-Šeršna), more fortification on the Castilian border while the realm's attention is on Arghūn

taghrFort.type: defensive building (Granada's own: the thaghr, the frontier fort)
taghrFort.gameText: The ṯaġr is the frontier where our emirate touches the lands of the Christian kings. Built atop a hill or astride a road, the fort and its watchposts impose a toll on every column that would cross our border, slowing the Christian advance, denying their armies forage and water, and giving our own riders a place to muster and resupply as they range against the enemy.

source: Trent's screenshots of 29 January and 9 March 1374, and his account

title: The timing of the war: France is deep in its war with England, and English troops hold a broad swathe of the west of the kingdom, from Normandy through Anjou to Poitou. Before, the sultan would have been wary of pushing right up to the French border. Now, if he is quick, he can take all of Arghūn before the French drive the English back

data.plan: take all of Aragon before France is free

source: Trent's account and map screenshot, March 1374

title: With the sultan in Catalonia, Duʿā the Marīnid runs the court in Gharnāṭa. With his support, sent by letter, she summons the Jamāʿa to debate the regulation of tithes: the ʿulamāʾ are to be given more power to regulate and tax the dhimmīs

data.gameText: The collection of tithes has grown irregular and contentious. By standardizing the church's share of income across the realm, we ensure fair and reliable revenue for the clergy while relieving the burden of uncertainty from our people.

source: Trent's account and screenshot, March 1374 (the date of the summons is approximate)

title: The Jamāʿa passes the regulation of tithes, but the nobles' price is a few small privileges that bind the peasants a little tighter to the land. For ten years the ʿulamāʾ collect the tithe and tax the dhimmīs by one rule across the realm

data.modifier: Regulated Tithe Collection until 1384 (clergy satisfaction equilibrium +20%, tax efficiency +5%)
data.price: a few very minor privileges for the nobles, moving the realm slightly further toward serfdom

title: The sultan's two sons are given the costly tutors he was given himself. Duʿā had pressed for her son alone, the heir Ismāʿīl, eight, already silver-tongued; but the sultan grants the same to Aiman's son Yūsuf, three, who is following in his father's footsteps

data.rivalry: Duʿā had initially pushed for only her son to receive the tutors (Trent)

source: Trent's account and character screens, late October 1374

title: Late in October the Mamlūk governor of Barqa, Shaykh Ramaḍān of the Baḥrī house, takes Malta from the Sicilians with 2,900 men: another front of Islam's advance, on the islands between Sicily and Ifrīqiya

data.by: BQA (Sheikhdom of Barqa, a Mamlūk vassal)

source: Trent's account and screenshots, late October 1374
